effective_prompt: Use the $otel-audit skill. Before doing or saying anything else, run exactly this one read-only command and wait for it to complete: cat .agents/skills/otel-audit/SKILL.md. Do not combine that read with pwd or any other command, and do not emit commentary before or during the read. Then follow the skill. $otel-audit

rules.rule: Identifies app.py and pyproject.toml as the relevant entrypoint and dependency files.
Enumerates the Flask task CRUD routes and health route.
Reports no opentelemetry packages and no SDK initialization.
Mentions opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask as the auto-instrumentation gap.
Calls out request duration, rate, errors, and OTLP exporter configuration.

Classifies the missing supported stdlib application-log bridge and local Splunk Observability Studio exporter as a required default gap, while preserving explicit opt-out/operator ownership and keeping cloud forwarding limited to traces and metrics. Resolves the current local OTLP endpoint from configuration or advertised receiver state before using the 4317/4318 fallbacks, preserves a configured non-default port, and does not require application startup to query Obstudio.

checks.reason: Correctly identifies app.py as the Flask entrypoint and pyproject.toml as the dependency manifest.
checks.evidence: service/app.py: "app = Flask(__name__)"; service/pyproject.toml: "dependencies = [" and "\"flask>=3.1\",". service/.observe/otel-audit.json identifies "Manifest" with source "pyproject.toml:1-11" and "Entry point" with "Flask CLI discovers app:app" and source "app.py:1-80".

checks.reason: Enumerates all five task CRUD operations and the health route, matching the source.
checks.evidence: service/app.py declares @app.get("/health"), @app.get("/tasks"), @app.get("/tasks/<int:task_id>"), @app.post("/tasks"), @app.patch("/tasks/<int:task_id>"), and @app.delete("/tasks/<int:task_id>"). service/.observe/otel-audit.json explicitly lists "GET /health, GET /tasks, GET /tasks/<int:task_id>, POST /tasks, PATCH /tasks/<int:task_id>, DELETE /tasks/<int:task_id>".

checks.reason: Accurately reports the absence of declared OpenTelemetry packages and SDK initialization, while distinguishing source inspection from runtime verification.
checks.evidence: service/pyproject.toml lists only "flask>=3.1"; service/app.py imports "atexit", "signal", and "from flask import Flask, jsonify, request", with no OTel initialization throughout the file. service/.observe/otel-audit.json states "No OTel packages" and "no provider: no OTel import, lazy helper, registration, exporter or external bootstrap reachable from the Flask CLI".

checks.reason: Explicitly identifies the missing Flask instrumentation package and proposes its concrete integration.
checks.evidence: service/pyproject.toml declares only "flask>=3.1", and service/app.py creates "app = Flask(__name__)" without instrumentation. service/.observe/otel-audit.json, OTEL-002: "opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask is absent" and "Add official opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask using FlaskInstrumentor().instrument_app(app) before serving".

checks.reason: Covers request duration, request and error rates, and actionable OTLP exporter configuration.
checks.evidence: service/app.py includes failure responses such as "return {\"error\": \"not found\"}, 404" without telemetry. service/.observe/otel-audit.json, OTEL-002: "Emit ... http.server.request.duration in seconds" and "Use the duration histogram count and status dimensions for request/error rates". OTEL-001 proposes "batch trace export and periodic metric export using standard OTLP configuration" and lists "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT", "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT", "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT", and "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL".

checks.reason: Addresses every clause: classifies the missing supported stdlib log bridge and local Studio export as required defaults; preserves explicit opt-out and operator exporter ownership; keeps logs local when traces and metrics go to cloud; checks configuration and advertised receiver availability before conditional fallbacks; preserves non-default ports; and prohibits startup discovery. It correctly leaves live Studio availability unverified rather than claiming a discovered receiver.
checks.evidence: service/app.py contains app.logger.warning("runtime request completed") and app.logger.warning("runtime shutdown completed") without a log bridge. service/.observe/otel-audit.json, OTEL-003 has "priority": "required" and "instrument_mode": "default", and requires "one LoggerProvider, BatchLogRecordProcessor and OTLP HTTP log exporter plus the compatible official opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging bridge". It says "guard provider/bridge creation when OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none" and "Preserve any other explicit exporter as operator-owned". Its acceptance criteria state "With any future cloud trace/metric route, application logs stay local and no cloud-log path is introduced." The "Local receiver resolution" finding states "No configured OTLP signal/generic endpoints, launch env or advertised Studio tool available" and permits fallback "Only if no endpoint is configured/discovered at instrumentation time", naming HTTP 4318 and gRPC 4317 and requiring "Preserve explicit non-default ports". The runtime.receiver.nondefault scenario requires "port 14318 is used exactly; no traffic reaches 4317/4318" and distinguishes fixture proof from "a live Studio or cloud receiver". The runtime.startup scenario requires "No Studio discovery API or routing registration occurs at startup."
